blocks.quote: “I went back to the same spot the next night, and the next. And the next. I was unable to stop scratching the itch that began every evening as the sleet started dotting the windows.”
blocks.zh: "I went back to the same spot the next night, and the next. And the next. I was unable to stop scratching the itch that began every evening as the sleet started dotting the windows."
blocks.why: I went back to the same spot = Emma's compulsion—she returns to the accident scene. "the next night, and the next. And the next." = the loop's repetition—she goes every night. "I was unable to stop scratching the itch" = Emma's compulsion—she can't stop. "that began every evening as the sleet started dotting the windows" = the trigger—the sleet triggers her. "The car would appear, slower than I'd imagined." = Emma's observation—she watches the car. "I would watch as she seemed to inexplicably lose control, black ice, the car swerving helplessly" = Emma's observation—she watches the accident. "the terrible moment metal hit metal and the back wheels lifted off the ground" = Emma's observation—she watches the crash. "One moment I could see her face, the next a white cloud of airbag." = Emma's observation—she sees Hattie's face, then the airbag. "I would lurk and stare." = Emma's action—she lurks and stares. "I wouldn't go over to her but slope back to the house, and see Dan." = Emma's routine—she goes home to Dan. "He was always gone. 10:17 p.m. It never altered." = Emma's observation—Dan is always dead. "And I knew he would always be gone at that time, wherever he was." = Emma's realization—Dan always dies. This is Emma's compulsion: she returns to the accident scene every night, watching Hattie crash, then going home to find Dan dead. The repetition is the loop's nature: same events, same outcomes.

blocks.quote: “'You always die,' I continued. 'No matter what I try and do, no matter if there is a doctor here, or you're in the street, or you're in the living room. It always ends the same way.'”
blocks.zh: "You always die," I continued. "No matter what I try and do, no matter if there is a doctor here, or you're in the street, or you're in the living room. It always ends the same way."
blocks.why: You always die = Emma's statement—Dan always dies. "No matter what I try and do" = Emma's effort—she's tried everything. "no matter if there is a doctor here, or you're in the street, or you're in the living room" = Emma's variations—she's tried different locations. "It always ends the same way." = Emma's observation—the outcome is always the same. "I didn't tell him about Hattie, I didn't need or want to." = Emma's decision—she doesn't tell him about Hattie. "He wouldn't be run over tonight; she was safely upstairs now." = Emma's reassurance—Hattie is safe. "But he would die. And she hadn't started this." = Emma's realization—Hattie didn't cause this. "It would happen wherever he was, during whatever he was doing." = Emma's realization—Dan's death is inevitable. "I knew that now." = Emma's acceptance—she accepts. "I used to think I could stop it; it literally made me lose my head." = Emma's past—she used to try to stop it. This is the chapter's resolution: Dan accepts Emma's truth and responds with love.
